title: Three questions at the table that aren't 'how was your day'
description: 'How was your day?' earns a one-word answer because it asks for a report. Questions that ask for a moment, a person or a surprise earn stories — and stories are what a family table is for.

body.heading: Ask for a moment, not a summary
paragraphs: Try: 'What was the funniest thing that happened today?' 'Who did something kind that you noticed?' 'What surprised you?' Each question points at one scene, and a scene can be told. A whole day cannot — which is why the summary question collapses into 'fine'.
Take turns being the asker, youngest included. The person who asks must also answer someone else's question; a table where only adults interview children becomes an interrogation, not a conversation.

body.heading: Keep a family deck
paragraphs: Write your best questions on cards and keep the deck on the table. Add new ones when a question produces a story worth retelling — those proven questions are family property now.
Retire questions that flop without ceremony. The deck evolves toward your family's actual humour and history, which is why it will outlast any printed list, including this one.

takeaway: Replace 'how was your day?' with questions that ask for a moment, a kindness or a surprise, take turns asking, and keep the proven ones as a family deck on the table.
